name: State of the Netherlands v Urgenda Foundation

jurisdiction.court: Hoge Raad (Supreme Court of the Netherlands)

description: The Urgenda Foundation and 886 Dutch citizens sought an order requiring the State to reduce greenhouse gas emissions (with direct effects on air quality and health) by 25-40% by 2020 compared with 1990 levels, in line with the 2007 IPCC report and with human rights protection obligations (Arts 2 and 8 ECHR).
outcome: Claim upheld in the final instance. The Hoge Raad upheld the decisions of the lower courts, ordering the State to reduce emissions by at least 25% by the end of 2020 compared with 1990. This was the first judgment in the world in which a government was legally bound to accelerate climate mitigation on the basis of human rights obligations; it created a global precedent for climate/clean air litigation.
